Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects pckt: A friendly way to send CKB OPEN ## Project Summary pckt is a red-packet style application built on CKB. A sender seals an amount of CKB into a single live packet cell governed by a custom Rust lock script, then shares a claim link. Recipients open the link and each claim consumes the packet cell and produces its next version, so the chain itself is the source of truth for who has claimed and how much is left. If all slots are claimed the packet terminates; if it expires first, the sender can reclaim the remainder. Three modes are supported: **fixed** (every recipient gets the same amount), **lucky split** (random non-last payouts with a contract-enforced 63 CKB minimum so no slot goes below cell-rent), and **timed unlock** (sealed until a wall-clock time, then everyone can claim). ## Tools used - **Contract**: Rust + `ckb-std` 0.18, `molecule`, `blake2b-ref`, `k256` (compiled to `riscv64imac-unknown-none-elf`) - **Frontend**: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite, `@ckb-ccc/connector-react` for wallet connect and transaction building, `@noble/secp256k1` for claim-secret signing - **Backend**: Rust + Axum + SQLite indexer, deployed on Fly.io (single shared-CPU machine + persistent volume) - **Hosting**: Vercel (frontend), Fly.io (backend), CKB testnet (Pudge) RPC + indexer - **CLI / deploy**: `ckb-cli` for keystore-signed contract deploys ## Current features - Seal a packet on-chain in fixed, lucky-split, or timed-unlock mode (2–50 slots) - Claim by link — the claim secret lives in the URL fragment so it never touches the backend - Lucky split with on-chain enforced 63 CKB per-slot minimum (just redeployed on testnet) - Timed-unlock packets that reject claims before the unlock timestamp - Reclaim flow for expired packets, wired into the sender UI - Sender-side dashboard: active packets, claimed activity, expired and reclaimable - Sender profile labels (backend-stored, convenience naming) - In-app notifications feed for claim

Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects CKBolt: Bitcoin Lightning ↔ CKB Fiber swaps, pay and get paid, both legs locked to one SHA-256 hash OPEN **Project Summary:** CKBolt links Bitcoin's Lightning Network and CKB's Fiber Network, so anyone can swap, pay and get paid between BTC and assets on CKB (native CKB, RUSD and cWBTC on testnet). A CKBolt hub runs an LND node and a Fiber node (fnn), quotes a price for each route, and locks both legs of every swap to one SHA-256 payment hash with hold invoices on both sides. Either the recipient is paid and the hub settles, or the payer is refunded; the hub cannot keep a payer's money without paying out. Users do not need their own Lightning or Fiber node: the web app runs a Fiber node in the browser (fiber-js), and any Lightning wallet can pay by QR code. Compared with Fiber's Cross-Chain Hub (CCH), which swaps one wrapped-BTC token at 1:1, CKBolt prices each route, so native CKB and CKB stablecoins work in both directions. Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects Cells (cellula.id): .cell names on CKB that can be paid, contracts public and reproducible OPEN **Project Summary:** Cells is a permissionless naming protocol on CKB. A `.cell` name is one live cell under a fixed type script; its records ride in the witness and the cell commits to their hash. What it adds over a lookup: the name can be paid. It publishes addresses per chain, a Lightning Address (`name@cellula.id`, forwarded unchanged to the wallet the name publishes), a Fiber node endpoint, and signed payment requests that carry bank details (SEPA, Pix, UPI) without putting them on chain. Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects CKB Kickstarter — Decentralized Crowdfunding Platform on Nervos CKB OPEN # CKB Kickstarter — Decentralized Crowdfunding Platform on Nervos CKB --- **Project Summary:** CKB Kickstarter is a decentralized crowdfunding platform built on the Nervos CKB blockchain, enabling trustless campaign creation, pledging, and fund distribution based on campaign success or failure. It follows an all-or-nothing funding model (Kickstarter-style): pledges are locked until the campaign deadline, and funds are either released to the creator (if the goal is met) or refunded to backers (if it isn't). All campaign and pledge data lives on-chain as CKB cells, with a lightweight off-chain indexer for querying and a Next.js frontend for the user interface. A working MVP is deployed on CKB testnet with full lifecycle support: create → pledge → finalize → release/refund → destroy. > Live Deployment: https://decentralized-kickstarter-kappa.vercel.app/ > GitHub Repository: https://github.com/alesfer001/decentralized-kickstarter --- ## Tools Used - **@ckb-ccc/core** v1.12.2 — transaction building, cell querying, RPC interaction - **@ckb-ccc/connector-react** v1.0.30 — wallet connection (JoyID, MetaMask Snap) - **ckb-std** v1.0 — on-chain contract runtime (Rust, RISC-V target) - **Next.js** 16.0.7 + **React** 19 + **TypeScript** — frontend framework - **Tailwind CSS** v4 — UI styling - **Express** 5.2.1 — indexer REST API - **better-sqlite3** 12.6.2 — persistent indexer storage - **Vercel** — frontend hosting - **ngrok** — indexer tunnel for testnet (temporary) --- ## Current Features ### On-Chain Contracts (Rust, RISC-V) - **Campaign Type Script** (`contracts/campaign/src/main.rs`) - Creation validation: funding_goal > 0, deadline_block > 0, status == Active, total_pledged == 0 - Finalization validation: Active → Success/Failed state transition, immutable field preservation (creator_lock_hash, funding_goal, deadline_block) - Destruction: allowed (lock s

Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects Cellora: a multi-tenant indexing and query service for CKB OPEN **Project Summary:** Cellora is a managed indexing and query layer for CKB, designed as a production data backbone for DApps that would rather not run their own full node, indexer and database stack. It normalizes blocks, transactions and cells into a PostgreSQL store with indexes tuned for the dominant access patterns (by lock hash, type hash, outpoint), exposes REST and GraphQL surfaces behind API-key auth and per-key rate limiting, and treats reorgs as a first-class case rather than an edge case. **Tools used:** Rust (Axum, async-graphql, SQLx), PostgreSQL, Redis, `ckb-jsonrpc-types`, `reqwest`, Docker / Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry + Prometheus. **Current features:** - Block polling loop against a CKB JSON-RPC endpoint (`get_tip_block_number`, `get_block_by_number`, `get_blockchain_info`) - Parser and writer that normalize blocks → transactions → cells - Live/dead cell accounting via `consumed_*` columns - One-transaction-per-block write path — the database never observes a partial block - Indexer-state tracking for tip recovery across restarts - Graceful shutdown on `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` **Planned features:** - REST API (blocks, cells, stats, health, cursor pagination) - GraphQL endpoint via `async-graphql` - API-key authentication (Argon2-hashed) with tiered rate limits backed by a Redis token bucket - Reorg detection and transactional rollback with an audit log - Range partitioning on the `cells` table by block number - Webhook delivery with HMAC signatures and retry queue - GraphQL subscriptions for live cell updates - Grafana dashboards and OpenTelemetry tracing - Dashboard for API-key management, usage charts, and a query explorer **Deployed on:** Dev chain today. Testnet is the next milestone, mainnet after reorg handling lands. **Link to repository:** https://github.com/Antismart/cellora **Link to hosted version of project:** Not yet hosted publicly —

A buyer can create and fund an escrow for a known seller, the seller can mark the work or goods as delivered, the buyer can release funds or open a dispute, and an arbitrator can resolve disputed escrows to either party. The project is not a marketplace or storefront; it focuses on the escrow workflow itself, with wallet-first identity, role-aware actions, indexer-backed escrow history, and a product UI supported by a separate protocol/studio interface. **Tools used:** - Rust for CKB script development - CKB RISC-V VM contract model - `ckb-std` - `ckb-testtool` - Docker reproducible contract builds - `@offckb/cli` for deployment tooling - CCC / CKB wallet integration - TypeScript - Next.js - React - Tailwind CSS - shadcn-style UI primitives - Postgres-ready escrow indexer storage - Neon/Postgres planned for hosted production history - Vercel planned for frontend hosting **Current features:** - Buyer-first escrow product UI - Wallet-first identity, no email/password registration - Testnet/mainnet network selection in the frontend - Buyer can create and fund escrow for a known seller - Seller can discover escrows they belong to and mark delivered - Buyer can release funds, cancel where allowed, dispute, or refund after deadline - Arbitrator can review disputed escrows and resolve to buyer or seller - Role-aware escrow discovery for buyer, seller, and arbitrator - Active and past escrow views - Terminal escrow history through indexer-backed recovery design - Escrow detail “deal room” with timeline, status, parties, actions, and receipt mode - Dispute evidence flow using off-chain evidence metadata and hashes - `/studio` route for protocol/debug/deployment workflows - Contract documentation, frontend documentation, and de

Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects Cellora: a multi-tenant indexing and query service for CKB OPEN **Project Summary:** Cellora is a managed indexing and query layer for CKB, designed as a production data backbone for DApps that would rather not run their own full node, indexer and database stack. It normalizes blocks, transactions and cells into a PostgreSQL store with indexes tuned for the dominant access patterns (by lock hash, type hash, outpoint), exposes REST and GraphQL surfaces behind API-key auth and per-key rate limiting, and treats reorgs as a first-class case rather than an edge case. **Tools used:** Rust (Axum, async-graphql, SQLx), PostgreSQL, Redis, `ckb-jsonrpc-types`, `reqwest`, Docker / Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry + Prometheus. **Current features:** - Block polling loop against a CKB JSON-RPC endpoint (`get_tip_block_number`, `get_block_by_number`, `get_blockchain_info`) - Parser and writer that normalize blocks → transactions → cells - Live/dead cell accounting via `consumed_*` columns - One-transaction-per-block write path — the database never observes a partial block - Indexer-state tracking for tip recovery across restarts - Graceful shutdown on `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` **Planned features:** - REST API (blocks, cells, stats, health, cursor pagination) - GraphQL endpoint via `async-graphql` - API-key authentication (Argon2-hashed) with tiered rate limits backed by a Redis token bucket - Reorg detection and transactional rollback with an audit log - Range partitioning on the `cells` table by block number - Webhook delivery with HMAC signatures and retry queue - GraphQL subscriptions for live cell updates - Grafana dashboards and OpenTelemetry tracing - Dashboard for API-key management, usage charts, and a query explorer **Deployed on:** Dev chain today. Testnet is the next milestone, mainnet after reorg handling lands. **Link to repository:** https://github.com/Antismart/cellora **Link to hosted version of project:** Not yet hosted publicly —

Instead of treating a sender-side payment-success response as sufficient proof, EventMesh records a signed, hash-linked application transcript between two operators, requires explicit acknowledgement of exact events, can bind receiver-verified Fiber payment evidence to the transcript, and lets both operators sign the same final commitment. Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects Owl Pilot & Owl Paymaster: automatic signing and sponsored fees for CKB apps OPEN ## Project Summary I'm building **Owl Pilot and Owl Paymaster**, two complementary pieces of infrastructure for CKB apps: Pilot reduces repeated signing prompts, while Paymaster sponsors eligible network transaction fees. Inspired by the experience of Cartridge Controller, Pilot lets users create or sign in to a passkey account inside an SDK modal, select app permissions and approve a spending allowance. A session key then signs matching transactions and scoped messages without repeated owner prompts. Developers describe permitted transaction effects through explicit templates. Owl Paymaster provides a fee pool, a quote-and-submit API, transaction validation, spending limits and durable retry/accounting records; it adds its own funds to each sponsored transaction without paying for the user's purchases or storage. Together, they aim to make CKB apps easier to use while retaining explicit consent, passkey-authorized recovery and clear boundaries between user funds and sponsored fees. The developer-facing goal is straightforward: **define the messages and state transitions your app needs, with explicit verification rules and transaction builders; let users choose which of those actions they trust Pilot to sign on their behalf.** Pilot handles the permission and signing flow, and Owl Paymaster handles eligible fee sponsorship. Developers still implement their app contracts, message verification and business rules; Pilot does not infer safe transitions from a human-readable name alone. ## Tools used - **TypeScript / Node.js**, with wallet SDK APIs, React components and the paymaster HTTP service/client. - **CCC (`@ckb-ccc/core` and the React connector)** for CKB transaction construction and existing-wallet integrations. - **Rust and CKB-VM** for the passkey owner, session account and sponsored transaction locks. - **WebAuthn / P-256 passkeys** f

Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects CKAutomata: payment automation and Nervos DAO Harvest on CKB CLOSED COMPLETED ## Project Summary CKAutomata is a non-custodial payment automation application for Nervos CKB. Its main feature, Nervos DAO Harvest, helps a user collect earned DAO compensation and place the original CKB amount into a new DAO deposit without manually tracking each withdrawal step. It also supports one-time scheduled payments and finite recurring payments. Users approve fixed rules through their wallet, while off-chain executors watch for eligible actions and submit transactions. I didn't spot an obvious principal-redirection path in the code I reviewed, although that isn't a substitute for an independent security audit. A couple of design issues stood out, both in DAO Harvest. **1. `min_compensation` can make a harvest cycle unable to progress automatically.** DAO compensation is fixed by the deposit and prepare inclusion headers, so it doesn't keep accumulating once phase one has completed. However, `validate_roll` rejects any claim where the calculated compensation falls below `min_compensation`. This means a late or otherwise poorly timed prepare by an approved executor, or a minimum calculated from overly optimistic yield assumptions, can leave the job unable to complete its normal roll transition. The owner can still recover the funds through the separate recovery path after maturity, so this isn't permanent loss of principal. But it is a liveness failure in the automated state machine.
